subject: Oumuamua interstellar object
title: Something Crossed Our Solar System in 2017, Then It Sped Up

scenes.text: Something crossed our solar system in 2017. Then it accelerated.
A telescope in Hawaii caught it on October 19th, already leaving. They named it Oumuamua: scout, in Hawaiian.
Up to 400 meters long, perhaps ten times longer than wide, tumbling end over end at about 196,000 miles per hour.
Its path gave it away: far too fast to belong to the Sun. It came from another star. The first interstellar visitor ever confirmed.
Then Hubble measured something odd. As it left, it was gaining speed, and there was no comet tail to explain the push.
The best guess today: hidden hydrogen boiling off its surface, like a tiny rocket. It will never return. It is still speeding away right now.

description:
In 2017 an object crossed our solar system, and as it left, it sped up.
Oumuamua was spotted by the Pan-STARRS1 telescope in Hawaii on 19 October 2017, already heading away from the Sun at about 196,000 mph (87 km/s). Its shape was extreme, up to about 400 metres long and perhaps ten times longer than wide, and its path showed it had come from another star, making it the first confirmed interstellar object. Hubble measurements then found it accelerating slightly as it left, with no visible comet tail; the leading explanation is hydrogen gas escaping from its surface.
What do you think Oumuamua really was?
first_comment: Oumuamua was only visible for about 11 days before it faded from even the biggest telescopes. If we could send a probe to chase it, would you want to?
